query: Protocol for detergent- and enzyme-free isolation of intact nuclei from whole zebrafish brain tissue for single-nucleus analysis
title: Nuclei Isolation from Whole Tissue using a Detergent and Enzyme-Free Method.
markdown:
## Protocol: Protocol for detergent- and enzyme-free isolation of intact nuclei from whole zebrafish brain tissue for single-nucleus analysis

### Overview

This protocol details the detergent- and enzyme-free isolation of intact nuclei from whole zebrafish brain tissue for single-nucleus analysis. The process involves euthanasia, dissection, mechanical homogenization using a specific kit, purification via centrifugation, staining with Hoechst dye, and sorting via Fluorescence-Activated Cell Sorting (FACS).

### Materials/Reagents

0.2% Tricaine solution in PBS; Ice-cold 1x PBS; Buffer A and Buffer B (provided in the nuclei isolation kit); Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA); Hoechst dye (1 mg/mL stock).

### Equipment

90 mm Petri dishes; 30 mm Petri dishes; Fishing net; Sharp razor blade; Forceps; Plastic grinding rod (provided in kit); Filter cartridge (provided in kit); Centrifuge (capable of 4 °C cooling); Vortex mixer; Fluorescence microscope (~405 nm laser excitation); Cell sorter (FACS); Glass bottom dish.

### Safety & Sterility

Maintain all reagents and samples on ice or at 4 °C throughout the procedure to preserve nuclear integrity. Use BSA-coated plasticware (tubes and pipette tips) to prevent nuclei adhesion. Ensure proper euthanasia protocols are followed when handling zebrafish.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation before tissue dissection

1. Prepare a 0.2% Tricaine solution in PBS for euthanizing the zebrafish and chill the solution on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. For euthanizing the zebrafish, prepare a 90 mm Petri dish containing 25 mL of the ice-cold Tricaine solution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare a 30 mm Petri dish for mincing the tissue. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Prepare ice-cold 1x PBS, allocating 10 mL per tissue sample. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Cool the centrifuge to 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Before starting the protocol, pre-chill Buffer A and Buffer B from the nuclei isolation kit by placing them on ice for at least 30 minutes prior to nuclei isolation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
7. Prepare a 5% BSA solution by dissolving 2 g of BSA in 40 mL of PBS to coat plastic reagents such as tubes and pipette tips. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->
8. Coat pipette tips by pipetting the 5% BSA solution into them 2-3 times, then air-dry the tips for 2 hours. Prepare 10 coated plastic tips per sample. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->
9. Coat collection tubes by filling them with 5% BSA solution, inverting them 3 times to ensure efficient coating, removing the solution, and air-drying the tubes upside down on clean tissue paper for 2 hours. Coat one collection tube provided in the kit per sample, and additionally prepare coated 1.5 mL tubes for nuclei collection after FACS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->

## Procedure

### Dissection of zebrafish brain

1. Carefully, take the zebrafish from the tank using a fishing net and place it into the Petri dish. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Euthanize the fish by leaving it in the Tricaine solution for 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Decapitate the animal using a sharp razor blade. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. Using forceps, gently break open the skull and remove soft tissues, skin, and bones from both the ventral and dorsal sides of the skull. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
5. Gently transfer the isolated brain into a fresh 30 mm dish containing ice-cold PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
6. Mince the brain into small pieces using a razor blade to facilitate loading the sample onto the spin column. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->

### Single nuclei isolation

1. Transfer the minced tissue to the filter cartridge provided in the nuclei isolation kit and add 200 µL of cold Buffer A to sensitize the tissue. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
2. Grind the tissue using the plastic rod provided by the kit for 2 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->
3. Add 300 µL of cold Buffer A and incubate the filter cartridge on ice with the cap open for 10 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S03 -->
4. Cap the cartridge and resuspend the tissue by inverting it 5 times. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S04 -->
5. Centrifuge at 16,000 x g for 30 seconds. During this step, cells are ruptured when passing through the filter, and the high-speed centrifugal force causes intact nuclei present in the flow-through to pellet at the bottom of the tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S05 -->
6. Discard the filter and resuspend the resulting pellet by vortexing vigorously for 10 seconds. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S06 -->
7. Pellet the nuclei by centrifuging the solution at 500 x g for 3 minutes. Carefully discard the supernatant, noting that the nuclei pellet is colorless. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S07 -->
8. Resuspend the pellet in 0.8 mL of cold Buffer B and centrifuge at 600 x g for 10 minutes. This step separates nuclei from membrane debris; the resulting colorless pellet contains the isolated nuclei. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S08 -->
9. Resuspend the isolated nuclei in 500 µL of PBS containing 5% BSA. Keep the nuclei suspension on ice to perform FACS after quantification. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S09 -->

### FACS Staining and Loading

#### Branch A: Control

1. Label two round-bottom FACS tubes as 'control' and 'stained'. The 'control' tube will contain unstained nuclei, while the 'stained' tube will contain Hoechst-stained nuclei. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->
2. Transfer 250 µL of the nuclei suspension into the 'control' tube using a BSA-coated pipette tip. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S02 -->

#### Branch B: Stained

1. Transfer the remaining 750 µL of the solution to the FACS tube labeled 'stained', add 1 µL of Hoechst dye to stain the nuclei, and mix by slow vortexing. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S03 -->

### FACS Acquisition

1. Load the unstained control sample into the cell sorter and record 5,000 events. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->
2. Load the stained samples into the cell sorter and record 5,000 events. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S02 -->

### Visualization of nuclei morphology

1. Confirm nuclear morphology by Hoechst staining. Remove 100 µL of the single nuclei suspension into a new tube using BSA-coated tips, add 0.1 µL of Hoechst (1 mg/mL), and gently vortex the tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S01 -->
2. Transfer the nuclei suspension to a glass-bottom dish for imaging. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S02 -->
3. Image the nuclei using a fluorescence microscope with laser excitation settings of approximately 405 nm (Violet wavelength). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S03 -->

### Draw FACS gates

1. Draw FACS gates that allow identification of single nuclei by comparing the Hoechst fluorescence signal between the control and stained samples. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S01 -->
2. Sort Hoechst-positive nuclei from the stained tube into a new 1.5 mL tube containing 50 µL of PBS with 5% BSA. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S02 -->
